module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Chvátal's Conjecture

*References:*

* [A Conjecture in Extremal Combinatorics](https://users.encs.concordia.ca/~chvatal/conjecture.html)
* [Chvátal's Conjecture and Correlation Inequalities](https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.08954)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Chvatal

variable {α : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]

/-- A family F of sets is Decreasing if it is closed under taking subsets. -/
def Decreasing (F : Finset (Finset α)) : Prop :=
    ∀ A B : Finset α, B ⊆ A → A ∈ F → B ∈ F

/-- A family F of sets is Intersecting if each pair of members has nonempty intersection. -/
def Intersecting (F : Finset (Finset α)) : Prop :=
    ∀ A ∈ F, ∀ B ∈ F, A ∩ B ≠ ∅

/--
If F is a decreasing family of sets of some finite type α, then there is some element
x of α such that the family consisting of all members of F containing x is an intersecting
subfamily of F with maximal cardinality.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem exists_maximal_star :
    ∀ F : Finset (Finset α), Decreasing F →
        ∃ x : α, ∀ G, G ⊆ F → Intersecting G → G.card ≤ { A ∈ F | x ∈ A }.card := by
  sorry

reformulations.difference: Chvátal's page defines an intersecting family as one that "includes no two disjoint sets". Pairs are distinct, so {∅} counts as intersecting. The page then excludes that one system ("The independence system that consists only of the empty set is an intersecting family and it has no nonempty star … no other independence system contains an intersecting subfamily that is larger than its largest star"). It also bounds each intersecting subfamily by the largest star: ∀ G, |G| ≤ max_x |star_x|. The Lean differs in four ways: (1) `Chvatal.Intersecting` is reflexive (`∀ A ∈ F, ∀ B ∈ F, A ∩ B ≠ ∅`, including A = B, so ∅ is never a member); (2) nothing excludes F = {∅}; (3) the quantifiers read ∃ x, ∀ G; (4) the ground type must be nonempty.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under the distinct-pairs notion, an intersecting family that contains ∅ must be exactly {∅}; every other intersecting family is also reflexively intersecting. Take a decreasing F with F ≠ {∅}. If ∅ ∈ G ⊆ F, then F contains some nonempty set T; pick y ∈ T, and the star of y has size ≥ 1 = |{∅}|. So on such F both notions give the same maximum. For F = {∅}, the reflexive notion allows only G = ∅, so the Lean statement holds there with no exclusion. (The distinct-pairs notion without the exclusion fails at {∅}; I checked this with #eval.) The two quantifier orders agree: ∀ G, |G| ≤ max_x |star_x| holds iff ∃ x, ∀ G, |G| ≤ |star_x|, taking x to maximise |star_x| over the finite nonempty α. If α is empty, every decreasing family is ∅ or {∅}, where the source's claim is trivial or excluded, so `[Nonempty α]` loses nothing; `#check` confirms `[Nonempty α]` is in the theorem's signature. Proved in Lean, with no sorry (axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound): for every α with [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α], the file's statement (which elaborates to exactly the type of `exists_maximal_star`) is equivalent to ChvatalPage α. ChvatalPage α says: for all F, Decreasing F → F ≠ {∅} → for all G ⊆ F with pairwise-distinct intersections, G.card ≤ Finset.univ.sup (fun x => {A ∈ F | x ∈ A}.card).

reformulations.difference: FKKK's Conjecture 1.1 (arXiv 1608.08954) says: "For any decreasing F ⊆ 2^[n], some largest intersecting subfamily has the form {A ∈ F : x ∈ A}". Its Proposition 2.1(a) uses max = |star|. The Lean only states the inequality: every intersecting G ⊆ F has G.card ≤ {A ∈ F | x ∈ A}.card. It does not say that the star is intersecting or that the maximum is attained.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every star {A ∈ F | x ∈ A} is intersecting, since x ∈ A ∩ B. So the maximum is always at least |star_x|, and the bound '≤' is equivalent to 'the star is a largest intersecting subfamily' (max = |star_x|). FKKK define intersecting as "A ∩ B ≠ ∅ for any A, B ∈ G", the same reflexive notion as the file (and as Mathlib's `Set.Intersecting`). Proved in Lean: FileStmt α ↔ FKKK α, where FKKK α := ∀ F, Decreasing F → ∃ x, Intersecting (star_x) ∧ ∀ G ⊆ F, Intersecting G → G.card ≤ (star_x).card.

sources_consulted: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1608.08954 (LaTeX source of Friedgut–Kahn–Kalai–Keller, 'Chvátal's Conjecture and Correlation Inequalities': Definitions, Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 2.1)
https://dwest.web.illinois.edu/regs/chvatal.html (D.B. West / H. Snevily, 'Variations on Chvátal's Conjecture', linked from Chvátal's page)
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/data/problems.yaml (entry for Erdős 701 = Chvátal's conjecture: status open, last update 2025-08-31)
http://users.encs.concordia.ca/~chvatal/conjecture.pdf (Chvátal 1974, LNM 411; downloaded but it is a scan with no text layer)
http://i.stanford.edu/pub/cstr/reports/cs/tr/72/292/CS-TR-72-292.pdf (Chvátal–Klarner–Knuth 1972 report, Problem 25; downloaded but it is a scan with no text layer)
review.notes:
I found no findings and no status issues.

What I checked:
- **Definitions.** `Decreasing` is the standard down-set (hereditary / independence-system) condition. `#eval` counts 3, 6 and 20 decreasing families on Fin 1, 2 and 3, which are the Dedekind numbers. `Intersecting` is reflexive, as in FKKK and Mathlib's `Set.Intersecting`. The star is `Finset.filter (x ∈ ·) F`.
- **Section variables.** `#check` shows that `[Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]` are all in the theorem's signature, so the degenerate empty-type case is excluded. That case is trivial or excluded in the source anyway.
- **Small cases.** I evaluated the whole statement with `#eval` for |α| ≤ 3 (all decreasing F, all G ⊆ F); it returns true.
- **The non-standard definition of "intersecting".** Chvátal's page uses distinct pairs and excludes the system {∅}. The Lean uses a reflexive definition with no exclusion. I proved in Lean that the file's statement is equivalent to the page's formulation and to FKKK's Conjecture 1.1. These are recorded as reformulations, not findings.
- **Status.** `research open` matches Chvátal's page (no resolution recorded) and the erdosproblems database (Erdős 701 open, last update 2025-08-31). erdosproblems.com itself returned a Cloudflare challenge to curl, so I took the status from the teorth/erdosproblems data file.

Minor remarks, not defects:
- The theorem docstring does not mention that α must be nonempty, but "some element x of α" already presupposes it.
- The `Intersecting` docstring says "each pair of members". That fits the reflexive reading the Lean uses.

Limitation: the 1972 Stanford report (Problem 25) and the 1974 LNM paper are image-only scans, so I could not read the original wording. I relied on Chvátal's own restatement on his web page, FKKK, and West's page. All three agree with the Lean up to the proved equivalences.
